title: Vistar: Enhancing the Perception Capability of LLMs under Imprecise IMU-Text Alignment

problem.claim: Manual natural-language annotation of high-frequency, low-interpretability IMU signals is particularly challenging.

gap.claim: A semantic gap remains between high-level visual semantics and low-level IMU vibrations, and precise IMU-text alignment remains difficult.

contributions.claim: Vistar is a self-supervised framework for IMU signal perception designed for large language models.
The framework combines offline cross-modal alignment with online retrieval-augmented generation.

Its offline training learns IMU encoders through hierarchical cross-modal contrastive learning using pretrained vision and language encoders as anchors, while online inference generates distilled textual descriptions from structurally related IMU-text examples.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Vistar as a novel self-supervised framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations on three multimodal datasets reportedly show that Vistar outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by up to 57.45% in IMU-to-text retrieval.
The authors report improvements of up to 31.90% in generated-text similarity with ground truths for IMU perception.

narrative_sequence.summary: IMU signals are difficult to describe manually because they are high-frequency time series with low interpretability.
Video-derived semantics do not fully align with low-level IMU vibrations, leaving a semantic gap.
Vistar combines offline cross-modal alignment and online retrieval-augmented generation to improve IMU perception.
The authors report gains over state-of-the-art baselines across three multimodal datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses pretrained vision and language encoders as anchors for hierarchical cross-modal contrastive learning.

interpretation.claim: When a modality is difficult to interpret directly, semantically richer pretrained modalities can provide alignment targets.

application.claim: Use cross-modal anchors and hierarchical alignment when developing perception systems for weakly interpretable sensor signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond the reported IMU perception setting.

source_observation.claim: Online retrieval filters similar text using structural relations of paired IMU samples before generating distilled descriptions.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval can compensate for residual alignment errors after training by conditioning generation on structurally related examples.

application.claim: Add structure-aware retrieval at inference time when learned cross-modal alignment remains imprecise.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the structural relations, retrieval procedure, or conditions under which retrieval helps.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three multimodal datasets or their task and evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not provide absolute metric values, baseline details, statistical variation, or ablation results.
The abstract does not specify the model architectures, training data scale, or computational requirements.
The abstract does not describe failure cases or limitations.
